walkthroughs.body_html:
Religious & Ethical Teachings about Relationships — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religious & Ethical Teachings about Relationships brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Religious & Ethical Teachings about Relationships.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which encyclical banned Catholic contraception in 1968?
options: Humanae Vitae
Rerum Novarum
Pacem in Terris
Laudato Si

mcqs.q: What is the maximum number of wives in Islam?
What does the Abrahamic covenant in Judaism involve?
options: God's promise to Abraham of land, descendants and blessing, in return for faithfulness — the foundational covenant marking Jews as a covenant people with responsibilities, not privileges.
Being 'chosen' means Jews believe they are superior to other peoples.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.

mcqs.q: How do Muslims believe the Quran was revealed?
options: Muhammad wrote the Quran based on his own teachings.
Through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) to Muhammad over 23 years; Muslims believe it is the literal word of God, not Muhammad's own words.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.

mcqs.q: What does Kant's categorical imperative require?
options: Acting only on maxims you could will to be universal laws, and treating people as ends in themselves, never merely as means.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Treat others how you would like to be treated.
